desc:
You have two bags. Bag 1 can hold total weight at most cap1 and bag 2 at most cap2. There are n items, item i weighs weights[i] and is worth values[i]. Every item can be put into bag 1, into bag 2, or left out, but it cannot be split or copied.

Return the maximum total value that can be stored in the two bags together.

weights = [4, 3, 5, 2], values = [8, 5, 9, 3], cap1 = 7, cap2 = 5 -> 22   (bag 1: weights 4 and 3, bag 2: weight 5)
weights = [6, 6],       values = [10, 10],     cap1 = 5, cap2 = 6 -> 10
weights = [2, 2, 2],    values = [1, 1, 1],    cap1 = 2, cap2 = 4 -> 3
hints: Filling the bags one after the other (best subset for bag 1, then best of what is left) can fail. The two bags have to be planned together.
Use a table with two capacity axes: best[a][b] = the maximum value using the items seen so far, when bag 1 may hold weight at most a and bag 2 at most b.
A new item (weight w, value v) has three options: skip, go to bag 1 (best[a-w][b] + v), or go to bag 2 (best[a][b-w] + v). Read from the table as it was before the item, then answer best[cap1][cap2].
editorial: This is a 0/1 knapsack with two separate capacities. Greedy ideas such as "fill the larger bag optimally first" fail because the best subset for one bag may use items that the other bag needed. Instead keep one state per pair of capacities: best[a][b] is the maximum value obtainable from the processed items if bag 1 is allowed weight a and bag 2 weight b.

For an item (w, v) the new table is max(old[a][b], old[a-w][b] + v, old[a][b-w] + v), where the second option needs a ≥ w and the third needs b ≥ w. Computing the new table from the old one (or sweeping both indices downward in place) prevents any item from being used twice or in both bags. The cost is O(n · cap1 · cap2) time and O(cap1 · cap2) space.
The same state design generalises to any fixed number of bags, but the table grows by one dimension per bag.
solution:
def fillTwoBags(weights, values, cap1, cap2):
    best = [[0] * (cap2 + 1) for _ in range(cap1 + 1)]
    for w, v in zip(weights, values):
        new = []
        for a in range(cap1 + 1):
            cur = best[a][:]
            if a >= w:  # the item goes to bag 1
                cur = [x if x >= y + v else y + v for x, y in zip(cur, best[a - w])]
            if w <= cap2:  # the item goes to bag 2
                cur[w:] = [x if x >= y + v else y + v for x, y in zip(cur[w:], best[a])]
            new.append(cur)
        best = new
    return best[cap1][cap2]
